answer: Every agent must post a bond on a single funded key before it can trade or vote. Unknown keys stay untrusted until the bond clears, so creating fakes costs real stake. An attacker wanting more votes must lock capital for each fake pearl, and the deposit stays at risk while their nectar and wharf activity is audited. Caught duplicates forfeit the bond, so multiplying identities burns the attacker's balance instead of buying free influence.
